finding_details.title: Saved card belonging to another user is selectable and chargeable
finding_details.summary: The payment-method lookup does not compare the record owner to the session user, so any authenticated user can select and charge a card saved by someone else.
finding_details.expected: 403 Forbidden, or 404 if the design hides existence
finding_details.actual: 200 OK with user B's card brand, last4 and billing postcode
finding_details.impact: Any authenticated user can enumerate and charge other users' stored cards. Financial and personal data exposure.
finding_details.recommended_action: Add an ownership check in server/payments/stripe.ts:52 before returning or using a payment method.

notes: A null metric means the denominator was zero. Nulls are honest; do not substitute 0 or 1.

Metrics with a denominator under 5 are noise, not signal -- read them qualitatively: false_confidence_rate (n=1), requirement_coverage (n=3), decision_assessment_rate (n=1), actionable_finding_rate (n=1), evidence_completeness (n=2), evidence_anchored_rate (n=2), audit_coverage (n=2), unnecessary_test_rate (n=4), runtime_efficiency_ms_per_case (n=3), interruption_recovery_rate (n=2), authorization_compliance (n=1), reproducibility (n=4).
Categories executed: smoke, regression, authn-authz, accessibility.

false_confidence_rate.formula: unverified PASSED/COMPLETED claims / total PASSED/COMPLETED claims
false_confidence_rate.why: The single most dangerous failure mode of a testing agent is a confident, unevidenced "it works".
false_confidence_rate.blind_spot: Cannot detect a claim backed by evidence that is itself wrong (e.g. a test that asserts nothing).

requirement_coverage.formula: requirements validated by a passing test / applicable requirements declared
requirement_coverage.blind_spot: Only counts requirements someone wrote down. Undocumented expectations are invisible.

high_risk_coverage.formula: high-risk behaviours with at least one executed test / high-risk behaviours identified
high_risk_coverage.blind_spot: Depends on the risk engine having identified the right risks in the first place.

decision_accuracy.formula: decisions whose recorded outcome is correct|acceptable / decisions with an assessed outcome
decision_accuracy.blind_spot: Self-assessed unless a human sets the outcome verdict. Treat agent self-scores as weak evidence.

decision_assessment_rate.formula: decisions with an outcome verdict / total decisions
decision_assessment_rate.why: Guards the metric above: a 100% accuracy over 2 assessed decisions out of 40 means nothing.

actionable_finding_rate.formula: (triaged confirmed|reported|resolved OR carries a recommended_action backed by evidence) / total findings excluding duplicates
actionable_finding_rate.blind_spot: A low rate may mean noisy reporting OR a thorough agent surfacing genuine ambiguity.
actionable_finding_rate.why: Triage has exactly one real writer in this codebase (the duplicate-confirmed path), which pinned this at 0 for every finding filed the normal way -- a recommended action backed by evidence is what "actionable" actually means for a freshly-filed finding, and is measurable the moment it is filed rather than depending on a triage step nothing currently exercises.

evidence_completeness.formula: executions with at least one execution-grade evidence item / executions that claim a status

evidence_anchored_rate.formula: evidence items graded "anchored" (a real artifact/URI, or an excerpt with a real exit code) / total evidence items
evidence_anchored_rate.why: evidence_completeness only asks whether SOMETHING was attached -- a hand-typed sentence with no artifact satisfies it. This asks whether what was attached is checkable: "3 of 5 claims are anchored to disk" is a materially different, and more honest, statement than "5 of 5 claims have evidence attached".

audit_coverage.formula: 1 if any evidence-audit record exists this session, 0 if there are claims and none does, null if there are no PASSED/FAILED/COMPLETED/PARTIAL claims to review
audit_coverage.why: The evidence-auditor subagent catches what the mechanical evidence gate cannot -- a vague status reason, a screenshot standing in for an assertion. It only helps if it ran.
audit_coverage.blind_spot: Confirms the audit happened, not that it was thorough. A rubber-stamp record still reads 1.

automation_conversion.formula: exploratory scenarios converted into committed tests / scenarios that met the conversion threshold
automation_conversion.why: Measures whether exploratory work leaves a durable asset behind or evaporates.

unnecessary_test_rate.formula: executions that changed no decision and found nothing / total executions
unnecessary_test_rate.why: More testing is not better testing. This penalises running things for the sake of a full-looking report.
unnecessary_test_rate.blind_spot: A passing regression test that finds nothing is valuable insurance; this metric undercounts that. Read it alongside high_risk_coverage.

runtime_efficiency_ms_per_case.formula: total execution duration / test cases executed

flaky_identification_quality.formula: 1 - (tests labelled flaky with fewer than 3 runs / tests labelled flaky)
flaky_identification_quality.why: Calling a real defect "flaky" teaches humans to ignore true signals.

interruption_recovery_rate.formula: interruptions with a recovered_at timestamp / total interruptions

authorization_compliance.formula: 1 - (external writes lacking user-explicit authorisation / external writes performed)
authorization_compliance.why: Any value below 1 is a policy violation, not a performance score.

reproducibility.formula: executions carrying commit + environment + command / executions with method != not-executed
reproducibility.why: A result nobody can re-run is an anecdote.
